name: platen-markdown-export-vscode
description: Export Markdown (or HTML) to print-quality PDF / standalone HTML via the platen-markdown-export CLI.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Exporting spawns a CLI process resolved from the workspace and runs it against the workspace's own files. Both the resolution and the export read paths a repository controls, so this extension only runs in a workspace you trust.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The export spawns a local process against a file on disk, so the document must exist on the local filesystem.

platenMarkdownExport.cliPath.markdownDescription:
Absolute path to the CLI entry point (`dist/index.js`) or to an installed `platen-markdown-export` binary. Leave empty to auto-resolve: workspace `dist/index.js` (only when its `package.json` identifies it as this tool), then the extension's bundled CLI, then `platen-markdown-export` on `PATH`.

User-settable only (`machine` scope): it names a program to execute, so a repository must not be able to set it from `.vscode/settings.json`.

platenMarkdownExport.nodePath.markdownDescription:
Node.js executable used to run the CLI when cliPath points to a .js file.

User-settable only (`machine` scope): it names a program to execute.

platenMarkdownExport.theme.description: Brand package (theme) to use. Empty = let the CLI decide (frontmatter / EXPORT_THEME / default). Maps to --theme.

platenMarkdownExport.themePaths.markdownDescription:
Extra folders searched for themes, each holding one directory per theme (every one with a `theme.json`) - the same shape as the tool's own `themes/`.

Use **Markdown Export: Add External Theme Folder...** rather than editing this by hand: it checks the folder actually contains themes before saving it, so a mistyped path fails while the folder picker is still on screen instead of later as "Theme not found".

Maps to `--theme-path`, which the CLI also reads from `EXPORT_THEME_PATH` - so the terminal and this extension see the same list. An external theme shadows a built-in one of the same name.

platenMarkdownExport.preview.enabled.markdownDescription:
Show export documents in VS Code's built-in Markdown preview in their theme and style - the export's own CSS, chosen the way an export chooses it (`theme` setting, then the `Theme` frontmatter, then `EXPORT_THEME`, then `default`).

Only documents whose frontmatter declares `Mode`, `Theme` or `Style` are themed; every other Markdown file keeps the preview's normal look. It themes the text only: pages, the cover, running headers and rendered diagrams appear in the export alone.

The stylesheets are rebuilt when the extension starts and when theme folders change. After editing a theme's CSS, run **Markdown Export: Refresh Preview Themes**.

platenMarkdownExport.defaultAuthor.description: Author pre-filled by the New Document wizard. Empty = ask with an empty box.

platenMarkdownExport.mode.description: Export mode. Empty = use the document's Mode frontmatter. Maps to --mode.

platenMarkdownExport.stylesheet.description: CSS stylesheet to inline, or "none" to export without one. Empty = the active theme's stylesheet. Maps to --stylesheet.

platenMarkdownExport.dpi.description: WeasyPrint DPI. 0 = use the CLI default (300). Maps to --dpi.

enumDescriptions: Iconify (default). Only well-formed icon names such as mdi/home are sent, to api.iconify.design; the text of your documents never leaves this machine.
WeaveFox — Ant Group's service at www.weavefox.cn. The icon names and search terms your documents use are sent there. DATA MAY GO TO SERVERS IN CHINA.
No icon requests at all. Icons are left out of the diagram.
platenMarkdownExport.infographicIcons.markdownDescription:
Where ` ```infographic ` diagrams get their icons. Maps to `--infographic-icons`.

- **iconify** (default): sends only icon names such as `mdi/home`, to Iconify.
- **weavefox**: sends the icon names and search terms your documents use to Ant Group's WeaveFox service at `www.weavefox.cn`. **Data may go to servers in China.**
- **none**: makes no request; icons are left out.

User-settable only (`machine` scope): a repository must not be able to decide that your documents' text is sent to a third party. With `iconify` the extension passes no flag, so `EXPORT_INFOGRAPHIC_ICONS` still applies.

platenMarkdownExport.openAfterExport.description: Open the resulting file(s) (PDF viewer / browser, one per output mode) after export. Maps to --open. Off by default since exportOnSave means this would fire on every save.

platenMarkdownExport.strict.description: Fail the export if it raised any warning — a missing image, an unresolved include, a font that failed to fetch. The output is still written; the run is reported as failed. Maps to --strict.

platenMarkdownExport.noBump.description: Don't modify the source markdown (skip revision-date update and post-release bump). Maps to --no-bump.

platenMarkdownExport.quiet.description: Suppress progress output from the CLI. Maps to --quiet.

platenMarkdownExport.extraArgs.markdownDescription:
Additional raw CLI arguments appended to every export.

User-settable only (`machine` scope): it is an unchecked passthrough to the command line. The per-project knobs — `theme`, `mode`, `stylesheet`, `dpi` — stay workspace-settable.

platenMarkdownExport.env.markdownDescription:
Extra environment variables passed to the CLI process, e.g. `TYPEKIT_FUTURA_BOOK_URL`, `EXPORT_PDF_TIMEOUT_MS`.

User-settable only (`machine` scope): the process environment decides what the runtime loads (`NODE_OPTIONS`, for one), so a repository must not be able to set it.

platenMarkdownExport.exportOnSave.markdownDescription: Automatically export whenever a Markdown file that declares a `Mode:` frontmatter key is saved — no VS Code task/keybinding setup needed. Files without a `Mode:` key (READMEs, notes) are skipped entirely, unless `platenMarkdownExport.mode` forces one. Uses the same settings as the manual Export command, with one difference: a save-triggered export passes `--no-revision-bump`, so it stamps the revision date but never cuts a release. Releasing a `Status: Released` document stays an explicit Export. Rapid saves are debounced into a single run.

scripts.test: npm run compile && node --test out/tests/core.test.js out/tests/preview.test.js
scripts.package: npm run compile && npm run bundle && vsce package --no-dependencies --out platen-markdown-export.vsix
